column12: Judgement on the comparator: the house convention. Savella is the closest marketed comparator in the same disease and setting: a branded reuptake inhibitor (milnacipran, the most norepinephrine-leaning SNRI) labelled for fibromyalgia alone and sold against generic duloxetine and pregabalin, which is where AXS-14, a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, will sit. It is the only fibromyalgia product in the book's CMS table. The spend covers 4.96 claims per beneficiary ($721 a claim), not a year, which matches the engine's stock recursion counting each start as a full year. The case for higher, and it is large: Axsome's own CNS brands read $4,686 (Auvelity) and $5,247 (Sunosi) per Part D beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand), 31% and 47% higher. Tonmya, the first new fibromyalgia drug in 16 years (launched 17 November 2025), lists at a WAC of $1,860 a month for the 60-count adult supply, $22,320 a year (Tonix, via pharmaphorum.com/news/tonix-launches-its-new-fibromyalgia-drug-us and panabee.com), and netted about $874 a prescription in Q2 2026 ($11.0mm over 12,592 prescriptions, Tonix Q2 2026 release, globenewswire.com 2026-08-10), about 2.4x Savella's halved $360 a claim. A new brand launched around 2029 is more likely to price near Tonmya or Auvelity than a 2009 brand. The case for lower: generic duloxetine and pregabalin cost a fraction of this, and payers may step AXS-14 behind them

column11: Liu Y, Qian C, Yang M, 'Treatment Patterns Associated with ACR-Recommended Medications in the Management of Fibromyalgia in the United States', J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2016;22(3):263-271, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2016.22.3.263, PMID 27003556 (MarketScan, 240,144 adults newly diagnosed 2009-2011): 'With the exception of duloxetine, discontinuation rates at 6 months were > 50% for all agents', milnacipran included, discontinuation being a supply gap of 90 days or more
column12: Judgement: constant hazard from the six-month figure, 1 - (1 - 0.5)^(12/6) = 0.75 a year. The '>50%' makes it a floor for milnacipran and pregabalin. Consistent with Savella's CMS series: 4.96 claims per Part D beneficiary a year (lookup.py demand Savella, 2024), about five months on drug, and with Axsome's own statement that over 50% of fibromyalgia patients discontinue within the first year (FY2025 10-K). The same rate is used to back Savella's new starts out of its CMS series in penetration_peak_pct, so the two stay consistent. Case for lower: duloxetine kept more than half its patients at six months, and FORWARD's randomized withdrawal design selects responders, which a label built on it may favour. Case for higher: esreboxetine's own adverse events (insomnia 15.7%, constipation 17.2%, dry mouth 15.7% on drug in the 8-week Phase 2; Arnold LM et al., Clin Ther 2010;32(9):1618-1632, doi:10.1016/j.clinthera.2010.08.003)

column12: Judgement on the timeline. Axsome gives no topline or resubmission date in its filings or releases (book filing texts and a September 2026 search checked). Topline around mid-2028, a resubmission in the second half of 2028 once the open-label safety study completes, and a standard 12-month review for a new molecular entity (reboxetine was never approved in the US) put approval in the second half of 2029, so 2030 is the first full year. Case for 2029: a fast resubmission after a March 2028 completion and an early action date. Case for 2031: any enrolment slip in a 620-patient withdrawal study, or a second FDA objection after an RTF history. LOE: no molecule patent date is filed. Axsome's FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-064267, patents section) lists only pending US and foreign applications for AXS-14, so the engine's default applies: 12 years from this launch year, 2042. No date is written here because none is filed

column11: Walitt B et al., 'Three-Quarters of Persons in the US Population Reporting a Clinical Diagnosis of Fibromyalgia Do Not Satisfy Fibromyalgia Criteria: The 2012 National Health Interview Survey', PLoS One 2016;11(6):e0157235, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0157235, PMID 27281286: 1.78% of US adults report a clinical diagnosis of fibromyalgia. Applied to 266,978,268 US residents aged 18 and over (Census SCPRC-EST2024-18+POP at 1 July 2024, the base epidemiology.csv uses for obesity): 4,752,213
column12: Not carried by the book (lookup.py pool Fibromyalgia and epidemiology.csv return nothing), so sourced here. Judgement: the clinically diagnosed population is the one a prescription reaches, and Savella's users, who set the peak, are drawn from it. A 2012 rate on a 2024 base. The criteria-based count from the same survey is almost the same size, 1.75% or 3.94mm of 225.7mm adults in 2012 (Walitt B et al., PLoS One 2015;10(9):e0138024, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0138024, PMID 26379048), but the two groups barely overlap: 73.5% of the diagnosed do not meet criteria and 73% of those meeting criteria have no fibromyalgia diagnosis. Axsome's 'approximately 17 million' (10-K; its deck cites Vincent et al. 2013) is a survey-based count not tied to a diagnosis, and is not used

column11: Kaur M, Rudnik J, Meisner P, Williams A, Lauwerys B, 'Prevalence and incidence of fibromyalgia and associated severity in the United States using MarketScan', Pain Rep 2026;11(4):e1451, doi:10.1097/PR9.0000000000001451, PMID 42238973, PMC13229459 (full text read): annual incidence of diagnosed fibromyalgia in adults 18 and over was 0.12% (95% CI 0.12-0.12) in 2020 in MarketScan Commercial + Medicare, defined on ICD-10-CM M79.7 (the fibromyalgia-specific code) as a first recorded code with none in the preceding 12 months, confirmed by a second code within a year, among adults continuously enrolled for 12 months. 0.12% x 266,978,268 US adults (Census SCPRC-EST2024-18+POP at 1 July 2024) = 320,374
column12: Judgement: the Commercial + Medicare adult rate applied to all US adults, and the latest year the paper reports. Replaces Weir 2006 (PMID 16755239), whose cases were first claims coded ICD-9-CM 729.1, 'myalgia and myositis, unspecified', a broad myalgia code; its 2,424,163 a year was 51% of the diagnosed prevalence, a two-year diagnosed duration for a chronic disease. This rate implies about 14.8 years (4,752,213 / 320,374). Case for higher: 0.16% in 2017 before the pandemic year (427,165 on the same base); 0.25% among Medicaid adults in 2020; the two-code rule misses patients not seen twice within a year (the paper's one-code rates are in a supplement not read). Case for lower: a 12-month washout counts some returning, already-diagnosed patients as new, and they already sit in the Walitt prevalence. Its effect on patients is contained: untreated_carryover_pct and penetration_peak_pct are re-derived on this basis

column11: Liu Y et al., J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2016;22(3):263-271, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2016.22.3.263, PMID 27003556: of 240,144 US adults newly diagnosed with fibromyalgia (ICD-9 729.1, MarketScan 2009-2011), 'Only 31% (n = 74,738) initiated a treatment with a prescription medication listed in the ACR guidelines' within a year. 74,738 / 240,144 = 0.3112
column12: Judgement: one filter, the share of diagnosed patients who start a guideline prescription drug, the population a prescription label reaches (the seltorexant seed's 'treated' filter, the same idea). It is measured on the same ICD-9 729.1 definition as the incidence. FORWARD's entry criteria are adults 18 or over with a fibromyalgia diagnosis (Axsome Q2 2026 deck, 8-K 0001193125-26-341206); no line or biomarker applies, and I could not open its full severity thresholds (the Pfizer Phase 2 required pain of 40mm or more on a 100mm VAS and a weekly mean of 4 or more; Arnold LM et al., Clin Ther 2010, PMID 20974319). Case for lower: the trials enrol patients meeting ACR criteria, and only 26.5% of the clinically diagnosed do (Walitt 2016, above); the label is expected to read 'management of fibromyalgia' like Savella's, and prescribers act on the clinical diagnosis, so that filter is not applied. Case for higher: 31% is the first year after diagnosis, and more of the prevalent pool has been treated at some point. The filter cancels against penetration_peak_pct, which is solved on this same basis

column11: Savella, CMS Part D (lookup.py demand Savella): 16,373 beneficiaries in 2023 and 16,606 in 2024. New starts in 2024 = 16,606 - 16,373 x (1 - 0.75) = 12,513. Medicare pool on this seed's basis: 53.1mm Part D enrollees in 2024 (KFF, Key Facts About Medicare Part D Enrollment, Premiums, and Cost Sharing in 2024, the book's brenipatide value) x (1.78% diagnosed prevalence + 0.12% incidence, Kaur 2026) x 0.31122 (74,738 / 240,144) = 313,991, less the 16,373 already on Savella = 297,618. 12,513 / 297,618 = 4.204%
column12: Judgement: a 1.0x multiple on Savella's 2024 capture. The same calculation gives 4.61% (2021), 4.26% (2022) and 4.07% (2023). Run through the engine's identity (k 0.574, midpoint 3, discontinuation 0.75), new starts peak near 54,000 a year around 2038 and the treated stock near 71,700 in 2039, about $256mm gross and $128mm net at the Savella price. Judgement also in applying the all-adult prevalence and incidence to Medicare enrollees; Kaur 2026 finds diagnosed prevalence rising with age to a peak at 70-79 in Commercial + Medicare, so the Medicare pool is if anything understated and this rate overstated. Case for lower, and it is quantified: Savella's US sales were about $102.9mm in the 12 months to January 2026 (IQVIA, cited in Breckenridge's generic launch release, March 2026), against $59.3mm of Medicare Part D spend alone in 2024, so Medicare is over half its sales; applying the Medicare capture rate to all adults sizes a Savella-equivalent at about $298mm gross (16,606 x 266,978,268 / 53.1mm x $3,572), 2.9x its measured national size. Generic milnacipran from March 2026 also cheapens the class incumbent. Case for higher: Savella in 2024 is 15 years past launch and barely promoted, and its Medicare users fell 13% from 19,099 in 2020; Axsome promotes to the same prescribers; Tonmya's prescriptions doubled quarter on quarter to 12,592 in Q2 2026 (Tonix Q2 2026 release); Axsome claims $0.5-1B peak sales for AXS-14 (Q2 2026 deck, 8-K 0001193125-26-341206). Case for lower also: AXS-14 arrives after Tonmya into a market led by generic duloxetine, pregabalin and gabapentin

column11: derived to hold the pool at its measured size, the method the remternetug and direclidine seeds use: retention = prevalence / (prevalence + inflow) = 4,752,213 / (4,752,213 + 320,374) = 0.9368
column12: JUDGEMENT. Fibromyalgia is chronic and the engine has no exit from the untreated pool, so at full carryover the M79.7 inflow would grow the diagnosed pool by 6.7% a year past its measured prevalence. Holding it stationary is the book's answer, and it implies 6.3% of the untreated pool leaves each year (remission, loss to care, death, or diagnosis lapsing). The case against: that exit is unmeasured, and on the 2017 incidence (0.16%) the same method gives 0.9175
